title: Media tab: one card per speaker or TV, playing ones first

steps.headline: Which layout should the Media tab use, so what is playing is easy to see and control?
steps.notice: Room boxes are gone: every speaker and TV is its own card, named like 'Destin's Room TV'. Playing first, then paused, idle, off, and speakers that are not responding last, dimmed.
steps.risk: All three re-sort when something starts or stops: a card you just paused moves down the page.

variants.label: Now playing hero
variants.summary: Big cards across the top for what is playing, with album-style colour, the title, large play, skip and volume. Paused ones sit under their own heading. Quiet devices become slim rows with one button: Play or Turn on.
variants.risk: The playing cards are tall, so a house with four things playing needs scrolling before you reach the idle devices.

variants.label: Stage and shelf
variants.summary: Playing and paused devices are wide cards with the controls on one line. Everything else sits on a shelf of small square tiles, each with one round button (play or power).
variants.risk: Tiles are small, so names and states wrap onto two lines; a long speaker name gets cut.

variants.label: One list, live rows
variants.summary: One simple column. A coloured bar on the left says the state: yellow playing, amber paused, grey idle, red not responding. Playing rows open up to show controls; the rest stay a single line.
variants.risk: The least dramatic: nothing is much bigger than anything else, so it is quieter to look at but less eye-catching.

steps.headline: When speakers play together, which layout makes them read as one thing?
steps.notice: Here Destin's Room and Roam 2 play one song. Each shows as ONE card or row, not two.
steps.risk: Grouped speakers share one title and one set of skip buttons; only volume can differ per speaker.

variants.label: Hero with a Together box
variants.summary: One big card. A 'Playing together' box inside lists each speaker with its own volume bar.
variants.risk: The tallest of the three, since every speaker gets its own bar.

variants.label: Wide card with name chips
variants.summary: One wide card with a linked 'Playing together' strip of speaker chips, and one volume bar.
variants.risk: You cannot set one speaker louder than the other from the card; that needs the Group bar.

variants.label: Row with a linked line
variants.summary: One row whose second line reads 'Destin's Room + Roam 2 together' with a link mark.
variants.risk: The smallest hint that two speakers are involved; easy to miss.

steps.headline: Press play, pause, skip and volume in each. Which one feels easiest?
steps.notice: These are the working page with a pretend house. The TV's remote is only a small round icon for now; its own design is decided separately.
steps.risk: Pressing pause or play moves the card to a new place in the list, which may feel like a jump.

variants.label: Now playing hero
variants.summary: Big cards for what is playing; slim rows for the rest.

variants.label: Stage and shelf
variants.summary: Wide cards on top, small square tiles below.

variants.label: One list, live rows
variants.summary: One column; playing rows open up, the rest stay one line.
